name: Enameloplasty (tooth reshaping)

lead: Enameloplasty is the removal of a little enamel to change how a tooth looks, such as shortening a pointed edge or smoothing a chip.
No clinical studies on the cosmetic use were found; related research concerns sealants and bite adjustment.

paras: A dentist uses fine instruments to remove and smooth enamel, changing tooth contours.
Wikipedia says removed enamel is irreplaceable and that dentin may be exposed.

lead: Enameloplasty, also called tooth reshaping or contouring, is the removal of small amounts of enamel to change a tooth's length, shape or surface, for example to smooth a chip or even out an edge.[1] Wikipedia's cosmetic-dentistry article says it gives fast results and can sometimes stand in for braces, but that removed enamel is irreplaceable and dentin may be exposed.[1]
The term also has clinical uses in the dental literature: widening fissures before placing sealants and adjusting bite surfaces to reduce muscle hyperactivity.[2][3]

paras: Cosmetic enameloplasty alters small details of tooth shape and is listed among cosmetic procedures that remove tooth material.[1]
The cosmetic-dentistry article warns that enamel cannot regrow and dentin can become exposed.[1]

No studies found on cosmetic tooth reshaping specifically. Related research on other uses includes laboratory studies of enameloplasty before fissure sealants, which examined sealant penetration and microleakage,[4][5] and a 45-subject study of computer-guided enameloplasty (immediate complete anterior guidance development) which reported reduced masseter and temporalis muscle activity.[2] These do not address appearance.
